aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.prompt: A BSW case manager at a neighborhood agency meets a client who has an eviction notice, an empty pantry, and two missed clinic visits. What is the BEST next intervention?

options.a: Link housing, food, and clinic resources and follow until each contact is made
options.b: Start insight-oriented therapy to explore why the client misses medical visits
options.c: Assign a psychiatric diagnosis so clinics will move the client ahead in line
options.d: Draft a county bill requiring every landlord to accept housing vouchers

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.explanation: Bachelor’s case management is brokerage plus follow-through: identify needs, confirm eligibility, make the links, and check that services actually started. Insight therapy and diagnosis sit at the clinical level, and writing a bill is macro work that does not fill tonight’s pantry or keep the apartment.

distractorExplanations.b: Insight-oriented therapy is clinical treatment, not BSW case management, which links and coordinates concrete services.
distractorExplanations.c: Diagnosis is outside typical BSW case-management scope and does not replace eligibility work and follow-up.
distractorExplanations.d: Legislative drafting is macro advocacy; this client needs individual linkage and follow-through on resources now.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.prompt: A client agrees to an intake at a community mental-health clinic but has dropped paper referral forms twice. What should the BSW do to complete the referral?

options.a: Fax the form and tell the client to call the clinic when they feel ready
options.b: Call the clinic with the client present and introduce them to intake staff
options.c: Close the case today because a written referral is already in the chart
options.d: Mail five clinic phone numbers and wait for the client to pick one

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.explanation: A warm handoff introduces the client to the receiving worker in real time, which raises the chance the appointment actually happens. A fax, a phone list, or a closure letter leaves the client to navigate intake alone—the pattern that already failed twice.

distractorExplanations.a: A faxed form is a cold referral; this client already failed that method and needs a live introduction.
distractorExplanations.c: Charting a referral is not the same as connecting the client; closing now abandons follow-through.
distractorExplanations.d: A resource list still requires the client to initiate contact, which is the barrier already documented.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.prompt: After a kitchen fire, APS asks a BSW where an oriented older adult with mild memory loss should live. The client wants to stay home; a neighbor already checks in daily. What setting fits least-restrictive practice?

options.a: Petition for locked skilled nursing because any fire means that level of care
options.b: Move the client to an out-of-county psychiatric hospital for a 72-hour hold
options.c: Arrange in-home supports and fire-safety changes so the client can remain home
options.d: Place the client in adult foster care today without reviewing other options

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.explanation: Least-restrictive practice uses the setting that meets safety needs with the fewest limits on liberty. This client is oriented, has natural supports, and wants to stay home, so in-home safety and services come before locked nursing, psychiatric hold, or an unreviewed foster placement.

distractorExplanations.a: A single fire does not by itself justify locked nursing when home supports can reduce the risk.
distractorExplanations.b: A psychiatric hold is for imminent mental-health danger, not a default after a kitchen fire.
distractorExplanations.d: Skipping option counseling violates self-determination and jumps past less restrictive home supports.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.prompt: A family-resource center asks a BSW to run a group for caregivers of teens with ADHD. Which format stays inside typical Bachelors scope?

options.a: An unsupervised process group that explores each caregiver’s childhood wounds
options.b: A psychodynamic group treating the caregivers’ personality patterns in depth
options.c: A lecture series with no discussion so members cannot trigger one another
options.d: A psychoeducation and support group on routines, resources, and peer coping

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.explanation: BSW group work is usually psychoeducation and mutual support: skills, resources, and peer exchange under agency structure. Unsupervised process or psychodynamic groups are clinical modalities. A no-interaction lecture is not group work; members need structured discussion, not silence.

distractorExplanations.a: Process groups that probe childhood material need clinical training and supervision beyond typical BSW scope.
distractorExplanations.b: Psychodynamic group treatment is an advanced clinical method, not a Bachelors psychoeducation group.
distractorExplanations.c: Group work requires interaction; a lecture with no discussion is teaching, not a support group.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.prompt: A client arrives at the BSW’s office the morning after an eviction, shaking and unable to name a plan for tonight. What is the FIRST crisis intervention?

options.a: Complete a three-generation genogram before any talk about shelter beds
options.b: Help the client stabilize, check immediate safety, then problem-solve shelter
options.c: Explore how childhood attachment explains the client’s reaction to the eviction
options.d: Write a six-month treatment plan before addressing where the client sleeps tonight

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.explanation: Crisis first-aid is stabilize, support, and then short-term problem-solving. Safety and tonight’s housing come before a full history, attachment interpretation, or a long-term treatment plan. Once the client is calmer and housed for the night, longer assessment can resume.

distractorExplanations.a: A full family history delays stabilization; crisis work secures safety and shelter first.
distractorExplanations.c: Childhood-root exploration is long-term therapy, not crisis first-aid in an eviction.
distractorExplanations.d: Long-range goals wait until the acute crisis—where to sleep tonight—is handled.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.prompt: Parents of children with IEPs at one elementary school cannot get interpreters at meetings. What is the BSW’s BEST mezzo-level advocacy step?

options.a: Testify alone before the state legislature on a new language-access statute
options.b: Coach one parent privately on legal rights and take no action with the group
options.c: Help the parent group present the interpreter gap at a school-level meeting
options.d: File a class-action lawsuit naming the district without trying local channels

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.explanation: Mezzo advocacy works with groups and organizations—here, the parent group and the school. Legislative testimony and class actions are macro. One-to-one rights coaching is micro and leaves the school practice unchanged for the other families.

distractorExplanations.a: State testimony is macro advocacy; the problem described is at one school, a mezzo target.
distractorExplanations.b: Private coaching is micro practice; mezzo work organizes the group toward the school.
distractorExplanations.d: A class action is a system-wide legal strategy, not the first mezzo step with one campus.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.prompt: A time-limited housing-navigation program ends in three weeks. The client’s voucher interview is scheduled for the week after the last session. How should the BSW handle termination?

options.a: Stop services this week because two remaining visits are not worth calendaring
options.b: Leave without notice so the client does not become dependent on the worker
options.c: Promise to keep meeting indefinitely after the grant and program episode end
options.d: Plan the ending, review gains, and make a warm handoff for the voucher date

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.explanation: Planned termination is a skill: name the end date, review progress, anticipate feelings, and arrange continuity. Abrupt stop or silent departure is abandonment. Continuing after the program ends is not honest and can create dual-relationship problems; the voucher interview needs a named next provider.

distractorExplanations.a: Remaining sessions are for closure work and the handoff, not optional extras to cancel.
distractorExplanations.b: Unannounced departure is abandonment; termination is discussed and planned with the client.
distractorExplanations.c: Extending past the funded episode is not a substitute for an ethical, planned handoff.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.prompt: A night-shift client needs groceries this week and cannot reach a pantry that is open only weekday mornings. What does the broker role require of the BSW?

options.a: Find a pantry with matching hours and eligibility and complete that referral
options.b: Teach thought-stopping so the client stops worrying about the empty cabinets
options.c: Represent the client at a fair hearing on an unrelated SNAP overpayment case
options.d: Coordinate the whole medical team even though food access is the stated need

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.explanation: The broker knows the resource map—hours, location, and eligibility—and makes a fit, not a generic list. Cognitive techniques, hearing representation, and medical-team coordination are other roles (educator, advocate, case coordinator) and miss the food-access request.

distractorExplanations.b: Thought-stopping is a clinical coping drill; the broker task is a matching food resource.
distractorExplanations.c: Fair-hearing representation is advocacy, and the hearing is unrelated to this week’s groceries.
distractorExplanations.d: Team coordination is case management of medical services, not the broker task for a pantry.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.prompt: In one breath a client lists an eviction notice, a court date, shutoff utilities, and a child’s IEP meeting. What should the BSW do first in the session?

options.a: Ask the client to pick one feeling to process for the rest of the hour
options.b: Help the client rank the problems and take one concrete step this week
options.c: Reflect both sides of ambivalence about whether any change is even wanted
options.d: Split the case among four agencies with no coordinating plan or follow-up

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.explanation: Partializing breaks an overwhelming pile into ordered, doable pieces so the client can act. Feeling-only process, an MI double-sided reflection, or dumping fragments on four agencies without a plan does not reduce the overwhelm or produce a next step.

distractorExplanations.a: Affect work without a sequenced plan leaves the concrete crises unaddressed.
distractorExplanations.c: Double-sided reflection fits ambivalence; this client is flooded with tasks, not stuck on whether to change.
distractorExplanations.d: Fragmenting the case is not partializing; partializing is a joint ranking and stepping method.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.prompt: During planning a job-search client says they “just want things to get better.” How should the BSW shape a usable goal?

options.a: Write “improve life circumstances” because a broad goal keeps every option open
options.b: Set the goal yourself: twenty applications this week whether the client agrees
options.c: Co-write a specific, dated goal such as submitting two applications by Friday
options.d: Keep the goal on feeling more confident, with no observable action attached

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.explanation: SMART goals are specific, measurable, and time-bound, and they are built with the client. “Things get better” cannot be tracked. Worker-imposed quotas violate self-determination. Feeling-only goals hide whether job-search behavior actually happened.

distractorExplanations.a: Open-ended wording cannot be measured; SMART goals name a behavior and a deadline.
distractorExplanations.b: Goals set for the client undercut buy-in; SMART planning is collaborative.
distractorExplanations.d: Confidence without an action is hard to verify; job-search goals need observable steps.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.prompt: A housing-navigation client misses a scheduled case-management visit. Agency policy allows outreach before closure. What should the BSW do?

options.a: Close the case the same day because one miss proves the client is unmotivated
options.b: Call the emergency contact and report that the client skipped the appointment
options.c: Wait until the client calls back so outreach does not look like chasing
options.d: Outreach per policy, ask about barriers such as transport, and offer a new time

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.explanation: A missed visit is a cue to outreach and barrier assessment—transport, child care, shame—not a character judgment. Closing after one no-show, telling an emergency contact, or waiting passively skips the engagement step policy and ethics expect.

distractorExplanations.a: One no-show is not proof of low motivation and is not, by itself, a closure trigger.
distractorExplanations.b: Emergency contacts are for emergencies; reporting a routine miss is a privacy breach.
distractorExplanations.c: Passive waiting skips outreach; workers initiate contact to identify barriers.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.prompt: A client must choose tonight between a shelter bed and staying with a relative who drinks. The BSW has openings at both. What does empowerment practice require?

options.a: Lay out the real options, risks, and supports, then follow the client’s choice
options.b: Book the shelter yourself because you already know which placement is safer
options.c: Require the client to follow the agency’s standard housing plan before choosing
options.d: Hold the resource list until the client meets two weeks of attendance goals

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.explanation: Empowerment is power with the client: real options, clear information, and the client’s decision, unless there is a duty-to-protect override. Choosing for them, forcing the agency script, or withholding resources as a reward is paternalism or coercion, not empowerment.

distractorExplanations.b: Picking the “safer” option for the client is paternalism, not empowered choice.
distractorExplanations.c: Compliance with a preset agency plan reverses empowerment; the client’s choice leads.
distractorExplanations.d: Using resources as a reward is coercive; access comes so the client can act on a choice.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.prompt: A parent whose child was just diagnosed with type 1 diabetes sits in the BSW’s office, overwhelmed by injections and carb counting. What intervention fits Bachelors scope?

options.a: Begin CBT thought records targeting the parent’s catastrophic thinking patterns
options.b: Give plain-language education on the regimen and link to a diabetes educator
options.c: Start DBT distress-tolerance drills as the primary work of this office visit
options.d: Interpret the overwhelm as unresolved grief from the parent’s own childhood

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.explanation: Psychoeducation plus a competent referral is BSW-scope intervention: explain the regimen in ordinary language and connect the family to a diabetes educator. CBT protocols, DBT skills modules, and childhood interpretation are clinical methods, not the first Bachelors response to a new medical regimen.

distractorExplanations.a: CBT thought records are a clinical protocol; the parent needs education and a specialist link.
distractorExplanations.c: DBT drills are advanced clinical skills work, not the BSW first response to a new diagnosis.
distractorExplanations.d: Childhood interpretation is psychodynamic therapy and delays practical diabetes teaching.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.prompt: After a home-based case-management visit, the BSW writes the progress note. What content belongs in the intervention documentation?

options.a: A character impression that the client is lazy about completing paperwork
options.b: The phrase “provided support” with no description of the actual service
options.c: The referral made, the client’s observable response, and the agreed next step
options.d: A verbatim transcript of every sentence spoken during the hour-long visit

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.explanation: BSW notes record services, not faux psychotherapy: what the worker did, what the client did, and the next step. Character labels, empty “support” phrases, and full transcripts fail audit, stigma, or usefulness tests. Language should be “case management / referral,” not “provided therapy.”

distractorExplanations.a: Character judgments are subjective and stigmatizing; notes stick to observable services.
distractorExplanations.b: Vague labels do not show what was done and fail most documentation standards.
distractorExplanations.d: Verbatim transcripts are not standard notes; documentation is concise and focused.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.prompt: A BSW is closing a housing-navigation episode because the client obtained an apartment and program time is complete. What should the discharge summary include?

options.a: Only the phrase “goals met,” with no next-provider or remaining-need detail
options.b: The entire intake packet in place of a concise closing summary of the episode
options.c: A judgment that the client has “poor insight” as the main closing content
options.d: Services used, remaining needs, and who will provide follow-up after closure

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-intervent.explanation: A discharge summary is a continuity tool: what was tried, what is still open, and who is next. “Goals met” alone, dumping the whole record, or a motivation slur does not let the next worker start. Planned closure still documents the handoff.

distractorExplanations.a: A closure reason without services, open needs, and a next provider breaks continuity.
distractorExplanations.b: Repeating the whole record is not a summary; discharge notes condense the episode.
distractorExplanations.c: Subjective motivation labels are not the core of a discharge summary.
